population: HCV genotype 1 (first-wave PIs; later agents pan-genotypic)
mechanism: Hepatitis C virus serine protease, NS3/NS4A inhibitor
note: HCV grows in no ordinary lab animal, so this class was carried from BILN 2061 (2003) to pan-genotypic cures on the genotype-1b replicon and NS3 enzyme assays, with the human-liver chimeric mouse as the only small-animal infection model.
label: NS3/4A protease inhibitors

engagement.note: Boehringer's NS3 inhibitor cleared subgenomic HCV RNA from replicon cells to undetectable within 14 days; no patient data yet.
engagement.short: PI clears replicon RNA in 14 days
engagement.quote: Treatment of replicon-containing cells with the NS3 protease inhibitor or IFN-alpha showed a dose-dependent decrease in subgenomic HCV RNA that reached undetectable levels following a 14-day treatment.
engagement.population: HCV genotype 1 (first-wave PIs; later agents pan-genotypic)

engagement.note: BILN 2061, potent in the genotype 1b replicon, cut plasma HCV RNA 2–3 log10 within 2 days in genotype 1 patients.
engagement.short: BILN 2061 cuts HCV RNA in 2 days
engagement.quote: Administration of BILN 2061 to patients infected with HCV genotype 1 for 2 days resulted in an impressive reduction of HCV RNA plasma levels, and established proof-of-concept in humans for an HCV NS3 protease inhibitor.
engagement.confidence: high; abstract-level (the 2–3 log10 figure is from the paper body, not re-read)
engagement.reason: Replicon potency matched patient viral-load drop
engagement.judgement: Viral-load fall is the direct pharmacodynamic read-out of NS3 inhibition, so it is scored as engagement; the same paper reports replicon EC50 and patient HCV RNA, so comparison_stated is true. Opener and comparison fall in the same year (Pause, Mar 2003; Lamarre, Oct 2003).
engagement.population: HCV genotype 1 (first-wave PIs; later agents pan-genotypic)

dose.note: Phase-1 dose ranging of BILN 2061 was anchored on its replicon EC50; no exposure–response comparison yet.
dose.quote: Here we identify a class of specific and potent NS3 protease inhibitors and report the evaluation of BILN 2061, a small molecule inhibitor biologically available through oral ingestion and the first of its class in human trials.
dose.confidence: medium; abstract-level — the trough-over-EC50 yardstick is in the paper body and in later practice (Kneteman 2006 dosed mice to 10× replicon EC50 at trough)
dose.population: HCV genotype 1 (first-wave PIs; later agents pan-genotypic)

dose.note: Across 14 PIs, plasma trough over protein-shifted replicon EC50 failed to predict 3-day viral-load declines; adding preclinical liver-to-plasma ratios rescued it.
dose.quote: For PIs, however, predicting VL decreases using the same model and the EC50,PS and day 3 Cmin was not successful; a model including LPR values and the EC50 instead of the EC50,PS provided a better prediction of VL decrease.
dose.confidence: medium; abstract only — full text blocked (PMC reCAPTCHA, Europe PMC empty), so the size of the miss is not recorded
dose.reason: Plasma target failed; liver ratio needed
dose.judgement: Scored contra by the letter of the rule: the standard exposure target (plasma Cmin over protein-shifted replicon EC50) did not predict PI viral-load declines in genotype-1 patients. The miss was in the conservative direction (PIs concentrate in liver, so patients responded more than plasma predicted) and the authors frame it as a scaling problem fixed by preclinical liver-to-plasma ratios; a lenient re-score could call the LPR-adjusted model 'same', but that model was fitted post hoc in the same analysis. Subscripts flattened in the quote (EC50,PS; Cmin).
dose.population: HCV genotype 1 (first-wave PIs; later agents pan-genotypic)

efficacy.model: Genotype 1b replicon + NS3 protease enzyme assays
efficacy.note: Replicons selected PI-resistant NS3 variants in culture, predicting resistance would emerge on monotherapy; no patient data yet.
efficacy.quote: Sequence analysis followed by transfection of replicons containing isolated mutations revealed that resistance was mediated by amino acid substitutions in the protease.
efficacy.population: HCV genotype 1 (first-wave PIs; later agents pan-genotypic)

efficacy.model: Genotype 1b replicon + NS3 protease enzyme assays
efficacy.note: Enzyme assays put BILN 2061's Ki 50–60× worse on genotype 2/3 NS3; genotype 2/3 patients responded weakly and variably, as predicted.
efficacy.short: Weak GT2/3 response matched enzyme Ki
efficacy.quote: A lower affinity of BILN-2061 for the NS3 protease of genotypes 2 and 3 HCV is most likely a major contributor to these findings.
efficacy.confidence: high; abstract-level for both Reiser 2005 and the enzyme prediction (Thibeault 2004, doi:10.1128/JVI.78.14.7352-7359.2004: Ki 80–90 nM genotype 2/3 vs 1.5 nM genotype 1)
efficacy.judgement: The in-vitro genotype prediction (Thibeault 2004) is the efficacy prediction tested here: BILN 2061 was strong in genotype-1 patients (Lamarre 2003) and weak/variable in genotype 2/3 (4/8 patients ≥1 log10, 3/8 no response), which Reiser attributes to the lower enzyme affinity. Note Thibeault's authors had read Ki <100 nM as 'potential' for non-genotype-1 patients; the data, not their gloss, predicted correctly. The genotype 2/3 arm sits outside the genotype-1 population but is the same drug and the same model, used as the negative control that shows the model discriminates; not scored 'neg' because no PI failed in patients for efficacy. Corroboration not used as source: the chimeric scid-Alb/uPA mouse (Kneteman 2006, doi:10.1002/hep.21209, 'paralleled responses in humans') and telaprevir-selected V36/T54/R155/A156 variants in patients (Sarrazin 2007, doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2007.02.037; the in-vitro comparison is in the paywalled body, not the abstract).
efficacy.population: HCV genotype 1 (first-wave PIs; later agents pan-genotypic)

safety.model: Human-liver chimeric uPA-SCID mouse / rhesus monkey toxicology
safety.note: Mouse and monkey cardiotoxicity flagged BILN 2061 and halted it after 2-day patient dosing; the flag was never tested in patients.
safety.quote: A 4-day treatment with BILN 2061 of HCV genotype-1b infected chimeric animals reduced the viral load by >100-fold, but concomitant clinical and ultrastructural signs of cardiotoxicity appeared.
safety.confidence: high; abstract-level. The rhesus 28-day finding (myocardial vacuolation at 1,000 mg/kg/day) is in Stoltz 2011, doi:10.1177/0192623311398276; its abstract dates it only as 'subsequent' to the 2003 proof-of-principle
safety.judgement: Flag without a patient comparison: patients received BILN 2061 for 2 days only and development stopped, so untested by rule 4. model_first_use_year is the first peer-reviewed primary I could verify (2007); the rhesus studies themselves predate it (~2004) but no primary source pins the year.
safety.population: HCV genotype 1 (first-wave PIs; later agents pan-genotypic)

safety.note: Rat predicted degenerative testicular toxicity at 0.17× clinical exposure; dogs and patients' hormonal biomarkers showed none.
safety.short: Rat testicular toxicity absent in patients
safety.quote: Degenerative testicular toxicity was not observed in chronic toxicity studies in the dog. Furthermore, mean changes in proposed hormonal biomarkers of testicular toxicity among subjects who received telaprevir were comparable to placebo.
safety.confidence: high; label section 13.1 read in full from the accessdata PDF (two consecutive sentences quoted, 32 words)
safety.reason: Rat testicular signal not seen in patients
safety.judgement: Scored contra by the letter of the rule: the rat predicted testicular toxicity at 0.17× the clinical exposure and the label states patients showed no signal. Lenient re-score could be 'same' for the two-species package (dog silent, patients clean) and the patient read-out is hormonal biomarkers, not histology. The bigger telaprevir safety story — anemia and severe skin reactions (SJS/DRESS, boxed warning added 2012) — has no animal counterpart in the 2011 label, which carries no section 13.2; that silence is not scored because no primary source states the comparison.
safety.population: HCV genotype 1 (first-wave PIs; later agents pan-genotypic)
